A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same MuSC research, with readable text, equations, tables, figures and complete Appendices A-D. Corresponding content can be matched reliably despite additions and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original instruction-following experiments, capability evaluations and ablations in Sections 4-5 and Appendices B and D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds Qwen2.5 model-size evaluations, DPO ablation results and a human toxicity audit.

M1.justification: The constraint decomposition, dropout, recombination and response-generation pipeline remains unchanged, as does calibrated entropy-weighted preference optimization. Section 3 and Appendix A introduce no revised algorithm or training objective.

E1.justification: The training sources and instruction-following and fundamental-capability benchmarks are retained. Ethical Considerations adds toxicity assessment of generated instructions and responses, extending evaluation to a limited data-safety task.

E2.justification: Table 4 expands the optimizer comparison from SimPO and IPO to include DPO with and without fine-grained contrast. The main benchmark comparator roster, including Self-Reward with GPT-4, was already present in v1 and remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.6 substantially broadens the evaluated model-size range beyond the original 7-8B models through Qwen2.5-Instruct configurations at 1.5B, 3B, 14B and 32B. A new human evaluation protocol uses three graduate annotators to inspect 200 randomly selected samples, 100 from each original model. Existing benchmark metrics and Appendix A settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds analyses of generalization across model sizes and toxicity in generated training data, and extends the token-contrast ablation to DPO in Table 4. These broaden the questions examined beyond v1's retained confidence-metric, noising, capability-retention and training-dynamics analyses.

E5.justification: Section 5.3 newly states that performance differences among xPO methods were not statistically significant. This introduces qualitative uncertainty reporting, but neither a test procedure nor p-values, confidence intervals or repeated-run information accompanies the statement.

E6.justification: New Table 6 supplies baseline-versus-MuSC results across four Qwen2.5 sizes; for example, the 3B model's AlpacaEval2 LC score is 27.44 before MuSC and 30.64 after it. v3 also adds DPO ablation results and reports no toxic instances among 200 inspected samples. Matched results from the earlier experiments and appendices retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and objectives in Section 3 and the token-level DPO derivations and dynamic-weight proof in Appendix C are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: multi-granularity self-contrastive alignment without stronger-model supervision and improvements in complex and general instruction following. The added experiments support these claims without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations concerning selected-token overconfidence, interprets the new results as evidence of model-size scalability, and explains the emphasis on DPO. Ethical Considerations newly identifies possible forgetting of safety alignment and recommends incorporating safe alignment samples; the existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: Table 5 newly identifies the previously indistinguishable MuSC result blocks as SelfInst and PreInst, clarifying which settings produced the existing numbers. Appendix A's hyperparameters, hardware and processing details, the prompt templates and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Several introductory survey citations are replaced by references concerning reasoning, factuality, long-context modeling and code critique. ComplexBench's attribution changes from He et al. to the newly included Wen et al. reference. The substantive related-work positioning remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds Section 5.6, Ethical Considerations and Acknowledgements, alongside short explanatory additions and an affiliation update. Most prose, the main narrative sequence and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: Table 4 gains DPO rows, a new model-size Table 6 is inserted, and Table 5 gains setting labels and a caption explaining its existing bold and gray formatting. Subsequent tables are renumbered and nearby text reflows; the figures and prompt displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens empirical support through evaluations beyond 7-8B models, additional DPO ablations and a small human toxicity audit, while clarifying previously ambiguous result labels. These are useful extensions to an otherwise stable paper. Their benefit is bounded: the toxicity audit assesses generated data rather than post-training safety, and the new statistical-significance assertion lacks a documented test.
